agents.name: Rex
agents.note:
US-523 DONE (Sprint 70 / V0.29.25, 2/8). Kiosk watchdog -- the defense-in-depth sibling of US-522. Commit: feat: [US-523].

THE HEADLINE: I built ONE of the two signals the AC offered, and the refusal is the most important thing in this story. AC1 said 'e.g. AllocateRingBuffer error-rate spike, OR a CPU-pegged chromium with no state-file-driven repaint'. I built the marker-rate detector and REFUSED the CPU one, because neither half of it is groundable today: 'no repaint' is not observable from outside the browser (states_http_server SILENCES per-request logging at :183, so there is no access log to read a renderer heartbeat from -- and I would not widen that token-gated server while US-525 is working in it), and the CPU half alone has no post-US-522 baseline (Atlas's 39/31/24%-wedged vs 18/9/8%-healthy predate --disable-gpu, and software rendering raises healthy CPU by an unmeasured amount). Shipping a CPU threshold today = a fabricated number. So the bound is stated in three places (module header, architecture.md, completionNotes): A WEDGE WITH A DIFFERENT SIGNATURE IS NOT DETECTED. Two cheap grounded paths exist if the CIO wants that coverage: read healthy chromium CPU during the US-522 drill and threshold against the measurement, or add a page-side renderer heartbeat (Iris) which makes 'no repaint' genuinely observable.

THE FOOT-GUN I NEARLY WALKED INTO, worth internalising: systemd DELETES a RuntimeDirectory when the owning unit exits. The ledger needs a tmpfs dir, and /run/eclipse-obd was the obvious place -- but a Type=oneshot declaring RuntimeDirectory=eclipse-obd would have deleted that directory INCLUDING the live states/ every emitter writes and the state server reads, every 30 seconds. The watchdog gets its OWN dir. Second half of the same trap: without RuntimeDirectoryPreserve=yes a oneshot's dir is removed on EVERY exit, so the ledger would evaporate each fire, cooldown+budget would always read empty, and the watchdog would restart the kiosk on every single tick -- a flapper with green unit tests. Both are pinned by tests and I MUTATION-PROVED them (set RuntimeDirectory=eclipse-obd + Wants=eclipse-dashboard, watched exactly those two guards go red, reverted, re-verified clean).

THE INVERTED-DEFAULT INSIGHT: for a self-healing component the DANGEROUS default is 'act', not 'do nothing'. So six never-flap rules, one test each: (1) an INACTIVE kiosk is left alone -- `systemctl restart` STARTS an inactive unit, which would usurp the splash OnSuccess hand-off (dashboard.service.x11 A-1, no [Install] by design); (2) unreadable journal = UNCERTAIN never wedge (I-037); (3) the journal window is max(now-window, lastAttempt) so the errors that justified a restart cannot re-trigger the next tick; (4) cooldown 180s > the 60s window; (5) an hourly restart BUDGET -- once spent the watchdog STOPS restarting, logs ERROR and exits 2 so systemd marks the unit FAILED; (6) RECORD-THEN-ACT -- the attempt is written to the ledger BEFORE the restart fires, so an unwritable ledger CANCELS the restart instead of silently uncapping rules 3-5. That last one is the design point I would keep: a rate limit is only real if the action cannot outrun its own bookkeeping.

AC2 'must not mask a still-present freeze class' is met STRUCTURALLY, not by a log line. Every restart logs at WARNING and says in-line that US-522 was supposed to have removed this class; the budget turns a recurring wedge into a persistent, visible FAILED unit rather than an invisible restart loop. If this watchdog ever fires on the bench, that IS the signal that US-522 did not hold -- do not read a restart as good news.

PRIVILEGE: unprivileged. The restart rides the EXISTING polkit grant (deploy/polkit-rules/51-eclipse-service-control.rules already gives the Pi user the restart verb on eclipse-dashboard.service) so NO new privilege was added, plus SupplementaryGroups=systemd-journal so the journal read does not depend on journald's per-uid file split. That polkit grant is a classic two-correct-halves hazard -- revoke it and every watchdog test stays green while recovery is dead on the Pi -- so there is a test pinning it.

OWED, AND I DID NOT FAKE IT: the validationCriteria (simulate/observe a wedge on the Pi) is NOT done -- no live exercise this iteration. Note for whoever runs it: with US-522 in place a NATURAL wedge should be unreproducible, so drive the drill with `--error-threshold 1` (or inject a marker via systemd-cat) and assert restart-happens + logged + ledger caps repeats. Do NOT expect to reproduce the real freeze.

SCOPE: unit_manifest.py deliberately untouched -- it consistently EXCLUDES timer-driven oneshots (drain-forensics, orphan-cleanup, boot-progress are all absent), so following that precedent is the non-drift choice. If PM/Atlas want the watchdog in `obdctl status all`, that is a separate call. Rule 10 met in-sprint: architecture.md gained a 'Kiosk freeze class + wedge recovery' subsection covering BOTH stories (US-522 shipped without a spec update, so this closes that gap too), and I amended the A-1 paragraph that flatly said 'No watchdog/timer' -- still true as written, but it would read as a contradiction.

GATE, SYNCHRONOUS, COMMITTED BEFORE BOOKKEEPING (no TD-059 stall): RED first (ImportError, module absent) -> 43 logic tests + 18 install guards pass, FULL tests/deploy 397 passed (I touched deploy-pi.sh, so the whole contract suite ran), tests/pi/ops green, ruff clean on all 3 touched Python files. ONE PRE-EXISTING RED, NOT MINE: tests/lint/test_ralph_promise_tag_contract.py = TD-073 = US-529, IN THIS SPRINT. TD-075 also still stands (10 project-wide ruff errors outside touched files), so lint was applied per-touched-file. `make` is NOT on PATH on this box -- run `ruff check` directly and read the real exit code.

OPS GOTCHA for the next agent: a broad `pytest tests/deploy tests/lint ...` on this SMB share exceeds the 120s Bash default and gets auto-BACKGROUNDED -- which is the TD-059 stall by accident, not by choice. Pass an explicit long timeout and keep the gate in the foreground.

NEXT UP is US-524 (CMA 256M), the third leg of the F-124 freeze fix. Read its conditionalOutcome first: if the boot-config write is outside deploy's write-scope, emit a one-line CIO ops instruction rather than half-applying it.
